* 12. applyInheritancePreview
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/applyInheritancePreview
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-inheritance-api.js
:LINE: 45
:MINS: 1.4
:END:

Inheritance changes use an authoritative preview followed by one atomic apply. The browser confirms the exact orphan binding IDs and echoes the snapshot digest; a stale request never silently accepts a refreshed deletion set. Parent-edge variation creates a sibling source and reparents the target, preserving its own composition. All consumers of that target in the branch see the change; the original source stays unchanged. The graph partial owns availability and scope wording. See [[file:../../../docs/tutorial/07-optional-required-sealed.md][lesson 7]].

* 14. export-plan
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/export-plan
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/browser_plan.clj
:LINE: 366
:MINS: 2.7
:END:

The ordinary account menu, function picker and Explorer navigation trail use bundled graph plans for their local state or markup. This exporter resolves inheritance, bindings, and renames on the server and emits an ID-based plan for supported primitives; the browser does not resolve graph names itself. Shipped plans are generated during development. The generic editable-graph export takes a whole snapshot and remains unavailable under tenancy. Personal components instead use ~graphden.editor.components/export-current~, which authorizes every source dependency and exports only a bounded component plan. See the [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/ui-preview/README.md][graph-backed UI contract]].

* 18. mountRow
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/mountRow
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-explorer-graph.js
:LINE: 516
:MINS: 1.5
:END:

Presents one already-authorized Explorer function row through the same ordinary ~app.ui-explorer~ view as the kind toolbar. The native tree owns the function ID, navigation, selection, ARIA and action buttons; the graph owns the row body's markers, name, vault path and scoped style rules. Loaded rows share one runtime and one list stylesheet with namespace bodies. A personal toolbar view with no row surface falls back only for rows, preserving its valid toolbar selection and showing a diagnostic. Disposal follows native subtree removal, and the renderer budget applies per row, never as a cap on the loaded Explorer tree.

* 24. mountCanvasBody
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editor/mountCanvasBody
:FILE: resources/packages/app/editor/editor-passive-canvas.js
:LINE: 231
:MINS: 3.5
:END:

Mounts passive canvas bodies through one shared lifetime and stylesheet mechanism. The app.ui-canvas binding keeps its original display ABI; app.ui-canvas-values separately presents value labels, type chips and inherited type history over finite display facts. Native overlays retain Run, actions, service controls, edit guards, focus and geometry. All bodies share a checked scoped stylesheet; overlay removal disposes their renderers. Scope reconciliation retires old owner facts before refresh, while first preference hydration keeps bodies only within the same authenticated location. Personal markup cannot claim native controls or identities; a malformed surface selects the builtin component. Existing sanitized representation previews stay native siblings. Values styles stay in flow; one measured grid pass reserves card widths, edge labels and type-history row envelopes.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/app/editor/editor-passive-canvas.js::  function mountCanvasBody(owner, host, surface, facts, options = {}) {][resources/packages/app/editor/editor-passive-canvas.js:231]]

The public handler is composed in [[file:../../../resources/packages/web/crud-write/fns.edn][web/crud-write/fns.edn]]: parse, reject unsafe changes, apply the write, then invalidate and notify. The selected card's Run button delegates to the existing Inspector Run owner; it does not create another execution form. That form resolves typed inputs, keeps [[file:glossary.org::#term/effect][effect acknowledgement]] visible, and submits through this shared function. History, Trace path and Capture values are independent request options. Capture values requires tracing and explicit cost consent; cancelling consent clears that option. The submitted function UUID and generation identify this run. A new submission stops the previous poll, clears its result identity and ignores late replies; changing selection cannot relabel an earlier run. Pending runs use the same result host and cancellation path. Server execution checks remain authoritative.

Groups a trace's invocations by function UUID, keeping call counts, cache hits and timings. Trace path without Capture values records execution without return values. With capture enabled, the latest fresh invocation owns the displayed value, including null or false. A later invocation without a value clears an earlier capture; when its capture exceeded the budget, the badge explains that the value is unavailable. It never substitutes an older result or promises to recover data that was not captured. A shortened inline preview of an available value opens the complete captured value with keyboard access. The shared popover lifecycle provides Close, bounded placement, focus return and cleanup when its anchor disappears. Secret entries carry no value.

DOM, size, scroll and viewport changes coalesce into one requestAnimationFrame update; short finite CSS motion and native Web Animations reported by their owners keep updates running while active. Native motion must affect a declared step target; pause, cancellation or detachment ends frame following.
